newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones fell 29.07 points to 6,499.34. PLDT's ADR was down $0 1/8 at $58 7/8.
* On Wednesday, the peso closed at 26.288 to a U.S. dollar from 26.266.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 3,065.65, down 8.63.
* The Philippine interbank call loan rate was down at 10.8125 pct from 10.90625 pct.

* Power rates to increase by 10 centavos in the northern island of Luzon from November 27 to December 26 due to the 7.99 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) hike of the National Power Corp. Napocor said the increase was a result of the commercial operation of the 700-megawatt Pagbilao power plant in Quezon, north of Manila.

* The Manila Times says the government's budget surplus declined by 31.9 percent or 3.21 billion pesos to 6.85 billion pesos during the first 10 months of the year compared to the 10.065 billion pesos registered in the same period last year due to lower revenue collections.

* The Business Daily says Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc (Digitel) failed to stir the stock market as it made its debut yesterday with a closing price of 2.55 pesos a share, below its 3 pesos offer price.

* The Business Daily adds an affiliate of pulicly-listed Ultrana Energy and Resources Corp signed a $175 million financing agreement with Shanghai Electric Corp of China for the construction of 300-megawatt power plant in Pinamucan, Batangas, south of Manila.

* The Philippines Journal says the International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) has concluded negotiations with financial institutions for aa $45 million loan to partly cover the development cost of a port terminal in Karachi, Pakistan.
